# jsonata2js

> jsonata2js is a Node.js library that compiles [JSONata](https://jsonata.org) expressions into
> plain JavaScript functions at runtime. Each expression is parsed, optimised, translated to
> JavaScript source, loaded in-memory via `node:vm`'s `compileFunction`, and returned as a
> ready-to-call `JsonataExpression`. Evaluation is measured ~45-56x faster than the reference
> `jsonata` interpreter on a realistic analytical benchmark (9.5x-82x across more targeted
> per-construct benchmarks). All 1,686 cases of the official JSONata test suite pass. Zero
> required runtime dependencies, Node.js >= 18. MIT licensed.

Use it when you evaluate the same JSONata expression many times and want compiled-function
throughput instead of tree-walking an AST on every call — compile once at startup, evaluate on the
hot path. Install: `npm install jsonata2js`.

Key facts:
- **Compile then evaluate:** `jsonata2js.compile("Account.Order.Product.Price * 1.2")` →
  `JsonataExpression`; `expr.evaluate(data)` → a plain JS value (object/array/string/number/
  boolean/`null`, or `undefined` for JSONata's "missing"). The instance is reusable across
  evaluations and inputs; don't call `compile()` on the hot path. `compileAll(sources)` compiles a
  batch and reports every failure instead of stopping at the first.
- **Bindings:** inject `$name` values and `$name(...)` functions per evaluation
  (`evaluate(input, bindings)`) or permanently (`assign` / `registerFunction`); a per-evaluation
  binding wins on a name clash. A bound function is also a first-class function *value* — passable
  to `$map`, piped through `~>`, handed to another bound function.
- **JSONata libraries:** `compileLibrary({ name: 'jsonata source' })` compiles a set of bindings
  written in JSONata once and applies it to any expression with `useLibrary`.
- **Guardrails:** `setTimeout(ms)` and `setMaxDepth(n)` raise `U1001`; every error carries a
  JSONata error code (`JsonataCompilationError`, `JsonataEvaluationError`, `JsonataLoadError`).
- **Compiled-code architecture:** parse → optimise → translate → load. Paths compile in "value
  mode" over plain values wherever the `{v,p,b}` tuple representation is provably unobservable,
  aggregates such as `$sum(x.f)` / `$count(x[cond])` are fused onto the value stream, and every
  capture-free per-element callback is hoisted out of the evaluator so it is created once per
  compiled expression.

## Documentation

- [Documentation]({{ '/' | absolute_url }}): overview, install, API, bindings, libraries, error codes, performance, and the compile→optimize→translate→load architecture.
- [Install and quick start]({{ '/#install' | absolute_url }}): `npm install jsonata2js`, compile an expression, evaluate against data.
- [API]({{ '/#api' | absolute_url }}): `compile`, `compileAll`, `compileLibrary`, `JsonataExpression#evaluate/assign/registerFunction/useLibrary/setTimeout/setMaxDepth`.
- [Errors]({{ '/#errors' | absolute_url }}): the error hierarchy and the JSONata error codes each one carries.
- [Performance]({{ '/#performance' | absolute_url }}): measured throughput against `jsonata`, per-construct benchmarks, and how to reproduce them.
- [Error-code reference]({{ '/error-codes.html' | absolute_url }}): every code the compiler and runtime can raise.
- [Source on GitHub]({{ site.github.repository_url }}): code and README. MIT licensed.

## Related projects

- [jsonata-jvm-compiler](https://vlad-public-code.github.io/org.json-kula.jsonata-jvm-compiler/): the Java 21 original this library is ported from — same pipeline (parse → optimise → translate → compile → evaluate), same official-suite acceptance gate, a different host runtime. It is the compiler behind Valem's reactive engine.
- [jsonata2py](https://vlad-public-code.github.io/org.json-kula.jsonata2py/): the Python 3.11+ sibling of the same pipeline, generating Python source.
- [tracked-json](https://vlad-public-code.github.io/org.json-kula.tracked-json/): a Jackson `JsonNode` wrapper that tracks each node's absolute `JsonPointer` through every navigation; includes RFC 9535 JSONPath and RFC 6902 JSON Patch.
- [Valem](https://vlad-public-code.github.io/org.json-kula.valem/): a deterministic reactive computation runtime for AI-generated structured data models, built on the Java sibling compiler.
- [Valem sandbox](https://valem.run/): the hosted, zero-install demo.
